attack_quote: The issue was not caused, directly or indirectly, by a cyber attack or malicious activity of any kind.

contributing_factors.source_quote: Note how the query does not filter for the database name.
contributing_factors.text: The feature-file query did not filter by database name, so after the permissions change it also returned the columns of the underlying r0 tables, more than doubling the features.

contributing_factors.source_quote: When the bad file with more than 200 features was propagated to our servers, this limit was hit — resulting in the system panicking.
contributing_factors.text: The Bot Management module preallocates memory and enforces a hard limit of 200 features; the doubled feature file exceeded this limit and triggered an unhandled panic in FL2 Rust code.

contributing_factors.source_quote: The file was being generated every five minutes by a query running on a ClickHouse database cluster, which was being gradually updated to improve permissions management.
contributing_factors.text: Feature files were generated and propagated every five minutes; mixed deployment across ClickHouse nodes caused intermittent recoveries and failures, making diagnosis harder.

contributing_factors.source_quote: This feature file is refreshed every few minutes and published to our entire network and allows us to react to variations in traffic flows across the Internet.
contributing_factors.text: The feature file is refreshed every few minutes and published to the entire network, so the bad file reached every machine quickly.

contributing_factors.source_quote: While it turned out to be a coincidence, it led some of the team diagnosing the issue to believe that an attacker may be targeting both our systems as well as our status page.
contributing_factors.text: The team first suspected a hyper-scale DDoS attack, partly because Cloudflare's status page, hosted off Cloudflare, went down at the same time by coincidence.

contributing_factors.source_quote: This was due to large amounts of CPU being consumed by our debugging and observability systems, which automatically enhance uncaught errors with additional debugging information.
contributing_factors.text: Debugging and observability systems consumed large amounts of CPU enhancing uncaught errors, which increased CDN latency.

contributing_factors.source_quote: This backlog, in combination with retry attempts, resulted in elevated latency, reducing dashboard availability.
contributing_factors.text: After the feature file was restored, a backlog of login attempts and retries overwhelmed the dashboard until control plane concurrency was scaled.

fixes.source_quote: Hardening ingestion of Cloudflare-generated configuration files in the same way we would for user-generated input
fixes.text: Harden ingestion of Cloudflare-generated configuration files as for user-generated input.

fixes.source_quote: Enabling more global kill switches for features
fixes.text: Enable more global kill switches for features.

fixes.source_quote: Eliminating the ability for core dumps or other error reports to overwhelm system resources
fixes.text: Stop core dumps and other error reports from overwhelming system resources.

fixes.source_quote: Reviewing failure modes for error conditions across all core proxy modules
fixes.text: Review failure modes for error conditions across all core proxy modules.

root_cause.source_quote: A change to one of our database systems' permissions which caused the database to output multiple entries into a “feature file” used by our Bot Management system.
root_cause.text: A database permissions change caused ClickHouse queries to return duplicate feature rows, which doubled the feature configuration file size; the oversized file exceeded a preallocated feature limit in the proxy's Bot Management module, causing the proxy to panic and return 5xx errors.
